official.title: Postdoc Position in Digital Planning Framework for Circular and Climate Resilient Urban Environments
official.description_text:
Challenge: Enable integrated planning for circular & climate resilient buildings.
Change: Develop digital multi-scale decision-support workflows.
Impact: Support construction and renovation planning.
Job description
The Faculty of Architecture and the Built Environment of Delft University of Technology is hiring a Postdoctoral researcher to work on a recently awarded Horizon Europe project, entitled AURORA (Shaping safe, sustainable, and human-centered places) under the supervision of Assistant Professors Simona Bianchi and Olga Ioannou, and Associate Professor Maria Pregnolato.
The broader AURORA project aims at accelerating the transformation of the built environment towards climate resilience and circularity. The project has a strong social perspective aiming at both technological and governance innovation. It combines innovative construction technologies, digital workflows, multi-level governance approaches, and participatory processes to support the development and implementation of resilient renovation strategies. Through demonstration pilots across Europe, AURORA provides practical frameworks for municipalities, practitioners, and stakeholders to evaluate and implement sustainable construction and renovation pathways.
You will contribute to the development of AURORA resilient and circular strategies multi-scale assessment framework. You will do so by assessing and classifying existing products, product systems and building configurations in accordance with the AURORA assessment framework and the project’s demonstrator contexts. You will also establish data structures that enable the exchange and integration of this information within those contexts. You will ultimately develop a user-friendly, intuitive digital interface to enable decision-making of circular and resilient building pathways for built environment stakeholders (governance bodies, construction companies, and individual users). The developed digital workflows will be tested, and validated through pilot applications, ensuring applicability across different building typologies, spatial scales and data availability conditions.
Key activities include:
Assessing integrated construction and renovation strategies, covering structural systems, façades and building equipment across different building typologies, climatic conditions and hazard contexts.
Translating assessed technologies and pathways into decision-ready parametric datasets and a structured database, enabling direct integration into AURORA digital planning workflows.
Developing a user-friendly, intuitive, digital interface to enable decision-making between built environment stakeholders.
As a Postdoctoral researcher, you will collaborate with two research groups within the Faculty of Architecture and the Built Environment: Structures and Materials (restructgroup) and Building Design & Technology (architectural-facades-products), and one group within the Faculty of Civil Engineering and Geosciences: Hydraulic Structures and Flood Risk (hydraulic-structures-and-flood-risk). The position is funded for 18 months, during which the candidate will conduct postdoctoral research while contributing to the broader AURORA research program. The project offers opportunities to collaborate with leading European universities, industry partners, municipalities and public authorities working on circular construction, digital workflows and resilient urban development.
Job requirements
You have a PhD degree in Civil Engineering, Architectural Engineering, Building Technology, or a related field;
You have demonstrated experience working in one or more of the following areas: resilience planning, decision support systems, building technology, sustainability assessments;
Demonstrated knowledge of building and/or geographic information systems, data structures or software integration is a must;
You have excellent oral and written communication skills in English;
You are able to work independently  and as part of a team, and to build collaborative, interdisciplinary/transdisciplinary networks;
You are motivated to develop digital solutions supporting sustainable and climate-resilient built environments;
Work experience in multi-institutional projects is not essential but will be considered an asset.
TU Delft (Delft University of Technology)
Working at TU Delft means contributing to solutions that really make a difference.
For over 180 years, we have been training engineers who make an impact worldwide in companies, government bodies, or as entrepreneurs. Our alumni turn knowledge into concrete solutions for the challenges of today and tomorrow.
These challenges are changing rapidly. That is why we focus on themes such as energy, climate, digitalisation, artificial intelligence (AI), and smart mobility every day. Our education and research are directly aligned with what society needs now and in the future.
At TU Delft, our people make the difference. With their knowledge and curiosity, our staff provide a high-quality education and conduct pioneering research that extends beyond the campus. You will have the opportunity to take the initiative, work with others, and grow as a professional.
Working at TU Delft means join an international community of professionals and students. Together, we create knowledge, innovations, and solutions that help move the world forward.
Faculty Architecture & the Built Environment
The Faculty of Architecture and the Built Environment has a leading role in education and research worldwide. The driving force behind the faculty’s success is its robust research profile combined with the energy and creativity of its student body and academic community. It is buzzing with energy, with four thousand people enthusiastically studying, working, designing, conducting research and acquiring and disseminating knowledge. Our faculty has a strong focus on 'design-oriented research’, which has given it a top position in world rankings.
Staff and students are working to improve the built environment with the help of a broad set of disciplines, including architectural design, urban planning, building technology, social sciences, process management, and geo-information science. The faculty works closely with other faculties, universities, private parties, and the public sector, and has an extensive network in the Netherlands as well as internationally.

Conditions of employment
Duration of contract is temporary for 18 months.
A job of 38-40 hours per week.
A salary based on Scale 10 of the CAO for Dutch Universities with a salary between €3706 - €5760 gross per month based on a fulltime contract (38 hours), plus 8% holiday allowance and an end-of-year bonus of 8.3%.
An excellent pension scheme via the ABP.
The possibility to compile an individual employment package every year.
Discount with health insurers on supplemental packages.
Flexible working week.
Every year, 232 leave hours (at 38 hours). You can also sell or buy additional leave hours via the individual choice budget.
Plenty of opportunities for education, training and courses.
Partially paid parental leave
Attention for working healthy and energetically with the vitality program.
Will you need to relocate to the Netherlands for this job? TU Delft is committed to make your move as smooth as possible! The HR unit,
Coming to Delft Service
, offers information on their website to help you prepare your relocation. In addition, Coming to Delft Service organises events to help you settle in the Netherlands, and expand your (social) network in Delft. A
Dual Career Programme
is available, to support your accompanying partner with their job search in the Netherlands.  .

You can apply online. We will not process applications sent by email and/or post.
As part of knowledge security, TU Delft conducts a risk assessment during the recruitment of personnel. We do this, among other things, to prevent the unwanted transfer of sensitive knowledge and technology. The assessment is based on information provided by the candidates themselves, such as their motivation letter and CV, and takes place at the final stages of the selection process. When the outcome of the assessment is negative, the candidate will be informed. The processing of personal data in the context of the risk assessment is carried out on the legal basis of the GDPR: performing a public task in the public interest. You can find more information about this assessment on our website about
knowledge security.

ai.summary: Postdoctoral position in circular and climate-resilient building design at TU Delft, developing digital multi-scale decision-support frameworks and workflows for construction/renovation planning. Requires PhD in Civil/Architectural Engineering and expertise in building information systems, data structures, sustainability assessment.

thematic_fit.rationale: No meaningful thematic overlap. Position addresses circular construction, climate resilience, and building lifecycle design—a domain in architecture/civil engineering. Researcher's expertise is in immersive learning systems, spatial cognition, and collaborative interaction. While both involve spatial/environmental design, the posting's focus is material systems, building performance, and engineering workflows. No connection to learning, collaboration, or XR.

methodological_fit.rationale: Weak methodological fit. Position emphasizes building information systems (BIM), data structures, database design, and digital interface development for decision-support. The researcher has experience designing interactive systems (Unity/multiplayer) and conducting user studies, which could theoretically apply to interface design. However, the posting requires deep knowledge of BIM, building technology taxonomies, and construction workflows—highly specialized domains the researcher lacks. The methodological core is engineering and data systems, not human-centred evaluation.

growth_value.rationale: Limited growth value. Position would build skills in digital interface design and decision-support systems, which are adjacent to HCI but oriented toward construction/engineering rather than learning or immersive systems. Would not advance capabilities in spatial learning, collaborative immersive interaction, eye-tracking, or physiological sensing. Growth in parametric design and BIM would be novel but outside stated research trajectory.

strategic_value.rationale: TU Delft is priority-2 institution. Faculty of Architecture and the Built Environment is design-oriented and has strong research reputation, which is strategically valuable. Position is Horizon Europe funded (AURORA project), providing funding stability. However, the research group focus on structures, materials, and building technology is not aligned with human-centred XR or immersive learning. Networking would build architecture/engineering contacts but not HCI/design community connections.

eligibility_flags: Requires PhD in Civil Engineering, Architectural Engineering, Building Technology, or related field. Researcher has MSc in Creative Multimedia—does not meet stated PhD requirement and is not in a related engineering discipline
Posting requires 'demonstrated knowledge of building and/or geographic information systems, data structures or software integration'—researcher has no background in BIM, GIS, or building systems
Posting specifies 'experience working in resilience planning, decision support systems, building technology, or sustainability assessments'—researcher has no track record in any of these areas
risks: Credential and discipline mismatch: researcher lacks PhD in required field and has no building/construction domain experience
Knowledge gap in BIM, building technology, and sustainability assessment is substantial; would require domain retraining
Position targets construction/renovation practitioners; researcher's experience is learning design and spatial interaction, not building performance or lifecycle planning
Digital interface work, while potentially applicable, is embedded in unfamiliar domain (construction workflows) rather than learning or immersive design
Research group focus is on structures/materials/building tech, not human-centred design or XR—limited networking value for stated target trajectory
